suspects.name: Margaret 'Peggy' Vesper-Croft
suspects.role: The niece -- keeper of the house and of its worries
suspects.statement: In my room from half past eight with a novel and my sewing. Asleep before eleven -- I heard him wind the hall clock before bed, as he always does.
suspects.secret: IOUs and a final notice from a lending office; the Tuesday letter terrified her. She never came down again until morning.
suspects.lie: She heard him winding the hall clock -- a clock that had been stopped since the blackout.
suspects.redHerring: Her debts make inheritance look like motive; her scissors in the parlour look worse than it is.

suspects.name: Julian Ashcombe
suspects.role: The literary agent -- seller of things not entirely his to sell
suspects.statement: I left at ten sharp. We spoke of sales and nothing else -- I never heard of any memoir, and I never saw one.
suspects.secret: He sold two of Tobias's copies as restored Vesper originals; Edmund caught him and demanded the money back by Christmas.
suspects.lie: 'I never heard of any memoir' -- his pencil note will sit impressed on the study blotter (Act 3).
suspects.redHerring: His visit and the forgeries give him guilt, not the poison.

suspects.name: Dr. Helena Marsh
suspects.role: The family physician -- keeper of hearts, including her own
suspects.statement: I was at my surgery all evening. He rang at half ten about his drops; I told him to come Monday. I never left the house I was in.
suspects.secret: She came at his summons at 10:56 by the garden door, read pages 40 to 43, and dosed the decanter when he turned to pour. Ruth Marsh was her sister.
suspects.lie: Never left the surgery -- the tread prints, the bolt and the hay-and-honey smell of the ash will say otherwise.
suspects.redHerring: Her prescription is the poison's easiest source -- and the cheapest misdirection.

suspects.name: Tobias Grimm
suspects.role: The apprentice -- the pencil behind the published line
suspects.statement: Inking in the attic from half seven to midnight, then my cot in the basement. I heard thunder, and a clatter like a clock falling, a few minutes after half eleven. Nothing else.
suspects.secret: He ghost-drew the last two Hollow books at Edmund's direction, and his copies were the forgeries Julian sold.
suspects.lie: None that matters -- his half-finished sketch is the truth-teller: the line stops where the power died.
suspects.redHerring: The horn button on the stairs is off his coat -- lost days before, swept along.

suspects.name: Colette Beaumont
suspects.role: The housekeeper -- baker of bread, keeper of the one honest ledger
suspects.statement: Kitchen from half six. After the dark I baked through till the lights came. I found the garden door off the bolt at half eleven and bolted it -- thought I'd left it so.
suspects.secret: She has been skimming the housekeeping tin for her sister's debts -- she hid the page, and shame keeps her stories tidy.
suspects.lie: None about the night; her ledger is the most honest witness in the house.
suspects.redHerring: The burnt loaf -- she blames the blackout; the pantry lantern proves her out.
